item.title: Police investigating assault captured on CCTV inside hair salon
item.description: Police are investigating an assault involving a man and a woman inside a hair salon, which was captured on CCTV. A video circulating online shows the man assaulting the woman inside the salon.
item.content:encoded:
Police are investigating an assault involving a man and a woman inside a hair salon, which was captured on CCTV.

A video circulating online shows the man assaulting the woman inside the salon.

CCTV footage shows the incident occurred on the 2nd of this month.

Police say they are yet to determine the location of the incident and are continuing to establish the circumstances surrounding the assault.

Police are advising the public that anyone with information should call 1681.

item.title: SCC, FRA and Waterways to meet next week over persistent flooding behind MHCC
item.description: We will meet again with the Fiji Roads Authority, and Ministry of Waterways next week to determine a permanent solution to the persistent flooding behind MHCC in Suva. This has been highlighted by Suva City Council CEO Tevita Boseiwaqa after fijivillage News raised concerns about the flooding that has again occurred behind MHCC this afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
We will meet again with the Fiji Roads Authority, and Ministry of Waterways next week to determine a permanent solution to the persistent flooding behind MHCC in Suva.

This has been highlighted by Suva City Council CEO Tevita Boseiwaqa after fijivillage News raised concerns about the flooding that has again occurred behind MHCC this afternoon.

Boseiwaqa says the Council has already met with the Fiji Roads Authority and Ministry of Waterways to discuss the issue.

There is still no deadline on when this recurring issue will be fixed.

He says the area has an underground outlet issue, while most of the infrastructure is also ageing.

Boseiwaqa says a special drive has been initiated by the Minister for Works to look into the drainage and infrastructure concerns, with the FRA now coming onboard.

The area has experienced repeated flooding during periods of significant rainfall, with the existing drainage infrastructure unable to cope with the volume of water.

We have sent further questions to the Fiji Roads Authority and Waterways for details on the work required and when a permanent solution is expected.

item.title: Nadi resident raises concern over lack of ear and nose specialist at Lautoka Aspen
item.description: A Nadi resident is calling for an ear and nose specialist to be available at Lautoka Aspen Hospital, raising concerns that the hospital has been without a specialist for the past four months. The resident, who wished to remain anonymous, says around 60 people were waiting when he visited the hospital on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
A Nadi resident is calling for an ear and nose specialist to be available at Lautoka Aspen Hospital, raising concerns that the hospital has been without a specialist for the past four months.

The resident, who wished to remain anonymous, says around 60 people were waiting when he visited the hospital on Friday.

He says it is disappointing that patients are not receiving the services they need.

The resident says he also tried contacting the Ministry of Health, and they told him they do not know anything.

He says Aspen Hospital staff have been advising patients to travel to Suva for treatment, but not everyone can afford to travel or is well enough to make the journey to CWM Hospital.

The resident also told fijivillage News that patients are often given appointments for later dates and, at times, have to see SOPD doctors because a specialist is not available.

The resident is calling for immediate action, saying patients should not have to spend time and money travelling from Nadi to Lautoka only to find that the specialist is unavailable and they have to return on another day.

We have sent questions to the Ministry of Health.

item.title: Four days of celebrations begin on Thursday as Yat Sen marks 90/40 milestone
item.description: Yat Sen School will mark a major milestone this week as students, staff, families and former students come together to celebrate 90 years of primary education and 40 years of secondary education. The four-day Yat Sen 90/40 Anniversary celebrations will begin on Thursday with a Welcome Cocktail at Yat Sen School from 5pm to 10pm.
item.content:encoded:
Yat Sen School will mark a major milestone this week as students, staff, families and former students come together to celebrate 90 years of primary education and 40 years of secondary education.

The four-day Yat Sen 90/40 Anniversary celebrations will begin on Thursday with a Welcome Cocktail at Yat Sen School from 5pm to 10pm.

The celebrations will continue on Friday with a Cultural Night at the Vodafone Arena from 5pm to 10pm, showcasing the traditions and cultural diversity of the Yat Sen community.

On Saturday, former students, alumni, teachers and friends will gather at the Vodafone Arena for a Black Tie Gala Dinner from 6pm to 10pm.

The gala will honour the school’s past while celebrating its future, providing an opportunity for former students to reconnect, recognise achievements and reflect on the legacy of Yat Sen.

The celebrations will conclude on Sunday with a Family Day at the Yat Sen School grounds from lunchtime.
